items.title: Eiji Kitamura interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: But I’m Japanese and I didn’t know jazz, but when I get old now, Hank Jones, Teddy Wilson, Fatha Hines, Trummy Young, many great musicians. I respect all musicians.

ctx.x: Boy, you’ve played with the best of them.

When I heard Hank Jones the very first time, Hank played with the Benny Goodman Orchestra, Hank Jones. And he played very good. Oh he’s the best pianist. But I met Hank Jones. Hank says, “Teddy Wilson is the best pianist.” Hank says. But everybody says great musicians, best musician, best musician. But I’m Japanese and I didn’t know © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
jazz, but when I get old now, Hank Jones, Teddy Wilson, Fatha Hines, Trummy Young, many great musicians. I respect all musicians. I need respect.

items.title: Eiji Kitamura interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: toured together with “Fatha” Hines and his band, and I guest played. And he taught me many, many things.

ctx.x: And he backed me to Hawaii, and I played with Trummy. He taught me many, many things, improvisation, jazz. And then after I met Earl Hines, yes, and in Japan toured together with “Fatha” Hines and his band, and I guest played. And he taught me many, many things. Then after, Teddy Wilson, yes. Teddy was very sweet to me. And Teddy taught me how to make an introduction on the horn, the clarinet. He taught me. And many things he taught me, that any style’s okay, in your originality. Bebop’s okay, Swing’s okay,…
Right. Similar advice you got from Buddy DeFranco. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
